script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Morning, Sarah. September 13th, 2026 already. Time really flies when you're busy, doesn't it?
script.ja: おはようございます、サラさん。もう2026年9月13日ですね。忙しいと時間が経つのが本当に早いですね。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It does. Good morning, Alex, and welcome to The Daily Tanu-chan Show. You look like you need that coffee today.
script.ja: そうね。アレックス、おはよう、そして『今日のたぬちゃんショー』へようこそ。今日はそのコーヒーが必要そうね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Oh, I always need my coffee. Especially with my little one waking up at 5 AM recently. It's a new, very early phase.
script.ja: ああ、コーヒーはいつも必要ですよ。特に最近、うちの小さいのが朝5時に起きるようになってから。新しい、とても早い段階に入った感じです。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Five AM. That's a challenging phase to navigate. I'm just on my first quiet cup of tea.
script.ja: 朝5時。それは乗り越えるのが大変な時期ね。私はまだ最初のお茶を静かに飲んでいるところよ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Lucky you. Anyway, it's a bit overcast out there today, isn't it? Feels muggy, even for mid-September.
script.ja: 羨ましいです。ところで、今日はちょっと曇り空ですね。9月中旬なのに、蒸し暑い感じがします。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It is. High of 31.1 degrees Celsius, low of 23.0. Rain probability is only 29%, though. So probably just humid and sticky.
script.ja: そうね。最高気温は31.1度、最低気温は23度。でも降水確率は29%だから、たぶん湿気が多くてベタベタするだけでしょう。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Yeah, sounds about right. I guess that means no chance of cooling down for a while. Still feels like summer, even with the clouds. It makes my commute a bit slow.
script.ja: ええ、そんな感じですね。しばらくは涼しくならないってことか。曇りでもまだ夏みたいです。通勤が少し遅くなるんですよね。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It does. Did you see the news about the clothing company making character costumes? For popular mobile games?
script.ja: そうね。服の会社がキャラクターコスチュームを作るっていうニュース見た？人気のモバイルゲームのね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Oh, I did. Nutte and Axel Mark, right? That's kind of amazing, actually. People really love their cosplay, so I guess it makes sense.
script.ja: ああ、見ました。NutteとAxel Markでしたっけ？あれ、結構すごいですよね。みんな本当にコスプレ好きですもんね、だから理にかなってる気がします。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: They do. My daughter's friends are always talking about these characters. The dedication some people have to getting the details right is impressive.
script.ja: そうね。うちの娘の友達もいつもそのキャラクターたちの話をしているわ。細部までこだわり抜く人たちの熱意はすごいものよ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Yeah, I can imagine. It's a whole world. My kid just points at everything now. I wonder if he'll get into cosplay eventually, or maybe just want a giant cardboard box to sit in. Either way, it's a project.
script.ja: ええ、想像できます。全く別の世界ですよね。うちの子は今、何でも指差してますよ。いずれコスプレにハマるのかな、それともただ大きな段ボール箱に入りたがるだけかな。どちらにせよ、プロジェクトですよね。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Probably the box first. Then the cosplay. There was another piece about anime high school versus real high school. Did you catch that one?
script.ja: たぶん最初は箱ね。それからコスプレ。アニメの高校と実際の高校の違いについての記事もあったわね。それ、見た？

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Oh, I saw that headline. How it's different. Like, less school festivals in real life, I bet. And no secret clubs, probably. Or at least, none that I knew about.
script.ja: ああ、その見出し見ました。どう違うのか、ってやつですよね。現実には学園祭が少ないとか、秘密のクラブとかも多分ないんでしょうね。少なくとも、僕は知らなかったです。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Exactly. The article said Japanese animation has a *penchant* for teenage protagonists. It makes sense, they're always in school, aren't they?
script.ja: その通りよ。記事には、日本のアニメはティーンエイジャーの主人公を好む『ペンチャント』があるって書いてあったわね。確かに、いつも学校にいるものね？

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: A 'penchant'? What's that, like a strong preference or a special liking for something?
script.ja: 『ペンチャント』？それって、強い好みとか、何かに対する特別な愛着ってことですか？

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Yes, it means a strong liking or tendency for something. A specific inclination. So, they tend to use them a lot.
script.ja: そう、何かを強く好む傾向とか癖のことよ。特定の傾倒ね。だから、彼らはよくそれを使う傾向があるってこと。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Oh, I didn't know that word. Makes sense. Definitely a tendency. My son would probably agree. He watches a lot of that stuff, and he always points out how unrealistic some of it is.
script.ja: ああ、その言葉は知りませんでした。なるほど。確かに傾向ありますね。うちの息子もきっと同意するでしょう。ああいうのをたくさん見てるから、どれだけ非現実的かをいつも指摘してますよ。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: I'm sure he would. Mine too. It's an interesting contrast. Anyway, there was also something about beautiful ukiyo-e tarot cards. East meets West in that design.
script.ja: ええ、そうでしょうね。うちもそうよ。面白い対比だわ。ところで、美しい浮世絵のタロットカードについての記事もあったわね。あのデザインは東洋と西洋の融合よ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Right, I saw that. The pictures looked really cool. Tarot cards are really popular here now, aren't they? My neighbor actually reads them for fun sometimes, says it's just for self-reflection.
script.ja: ええ、見ました。絵がすごくかっこよかったです。タロットカードって今、日本でもすごく人気ですよね？うちの近所の人が、たまに遊びで読んでるんですよ。自己省察のためだって言ってますけど。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: They are. It's interesting how old traditions find new life, especially when they blend cultures like that. They've been around since the 15th century in Europe, but only became well-known here after World War II.
script.ja: そうね。古い伝統が新しい形で生き返るのって面白いわ、特にああやって文化が融合するとね。ヨーロッパでは15世紀からあるらしいけど、日本では第二次世界大戦後にようやく知られるようになったのよ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Wow, that's a long time. So much history. You know, speaking of old traditions, I just remembered what today is. It's kind of a unique one.
script.ja: へえ、そんなに昔から。歴史が深いですね。そういえば、古い伝統といえば、今日が何の日か思い出したんです。ちょっとユニークなやつです。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Oh? What is it? Something I should know about?
script.ja: あら？何の日？私が知っておくべきことかしら？

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: It's Men's Valentine's Day. According to the Japan Body Fashion Association. I just saw it on a calendar.
script.ja: メンズバレンタインデーだそうです。日本ボディファッション協会が制定した、って。たまたまカレンダーで見かけたんです。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Ah, yes. I'd forgotten about that one. Men are supposed to give women lingerie in return for their Valentine's chocolate. It was established quite a while ago.
script.ja: ああ、そうね。それ忘れてたわ。バレンタインのチョコレートのお返しに、男性が女性に下着を贈って愛を告白する日ね。かなり前に制定されたのよ。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Right! Lingerie. That's... a bold move. I feel like that's a pretty specific gift. You'd really have to know the person well to pick something like that out.
script.ja: そう！下着ですね。それは…大胆な動きですね。かなり具体的なプレゼントだと感じます。ああいうものを選ぶには、相手のことを本当によく知らないと。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: You definitely would. It was established in 1991, but I don't think it really caught on like White Day did. It never became a big thing.
script.ja: 絶対にそうね。1991年に制定されたけど、ホワイトデーほどは定着しなかったと思うわ。大きなイベントにはならなかったわね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: No, I guess not. I can't imagine many guys at my office doing that. Or even my friends. Maybe I'm just out of touch, but it feels like it's too much pressure to get it right.
script.ja: ええ、そうでしょうね。うちの会社の男性や、友達でもそんなことするなんて想像できないですよ。僕が時代遅れなだけかな、でも、正しく選ぶにはプレッシャーが大きすぎる気がします。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: It's a lot of pressure, especially when you think about sizing and style preferences. It's probably easier to just buy a nice dinner. Or some camping gear.
script.ja: すごくプレッシャーよ、サイズやスタイルの好みを考えると特にね。美味しいディナーをご馳走する方がたぶん楽よ。それか、キャンプ用品とかね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Camping gear! That's what I've been thinking about. I saw this new tent online, it's super lightweight and packs down so small. Maybe for my birthday next year, if I can convince my wife.
script.ja: キャンプ用品！それですよ、最近考えてたのは。ネットで新しいテントを見たんですけど、すごく軽くてコンパクトになるんです。来年の誕生日とかに、妻を説得できたらいいなと。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: A new tent sounds nice. My kids used to love camping and hiking when they were younger, but now they just want strong Wi-Fi and comfortable beds.
script.ja: 新しいテント、いいわね。うちの子たちは小さい頃はキャンプもハイキングも大好きだったけど、今は強いWi-Fiと快適なベッドがないと嫌みたいね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Yeah, I can imagine. Trying to get my little one outside is already a challenge, even for a short walk. He just wants to play with the remote control or chew on the dog's toys.
script.ja: ええ、想像できます。うちの小さいのを外に連れ出すのももう大変ですよ、短い散歩でもね。リモコンで遊びたがるか、犬のおもちゃを噛みたがるか。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: They all do that. It's a phase. You'll get back to those outdoor adventures eventually. Just a different kind for a while.
script.ja: みんなそうよ。一時的なものよ。いずれまたアウトドアの冒険に戻れるわ。しばらくは違う種類の冒険ってだけね。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: A different kind. Right. I keep telling myself that. I'm already daydreaming about a quiet weekend away, just me and my coffee, maybe a small fire.
script.ja: 違う種類の、ね。そうですね。自分に言い聞かせなきゃ。もうすでに静かな週末の休暇を夢見てますよ、僕とコーヒーだけで、たぶん小さな焚き火とか。

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Sounds peaceful. You'll get there. Anyway, I think we're out of time already. Thanks for the chat, Alex.
script.ja: 穏やかそうでいいわね。きっと叶うわ。とにかく、もう時間がないみたいね。アレックス、おしゃべりありがとう。

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: You're welcome, Sarah. Always a good way to start the morning. Have a good one!
script.ja: どういたしまして、サラさん。いつも朝の始まりに良いですね。良い一日を！

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: You too.
script.ja: あなたもね。
